sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Ehtesham Afsar Khan,Mahendra Pal Singh Gaur,R.U. Rinki Renu Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned Additional Government Advocate representing the State.

The instant second bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. has been filed on behalf of the applicant with a prayer to release him on bail in Case Crime No. 291 of 2019, under Sections 498A,
304B of I.P.C. read with Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Bhamora, District Bareilly, during the pendency of trial.
First bail application of the applicant was rejected by this Court vide order dated 20.03.2023 in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 17805 of 2022.

entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:

1

Main substratum of argument of learned counsel for the applicant is that the applicant is languishing in jail since 23.12.2019, but till date, his trial has not been concluded, whereas there is no delay on his part, therefore, he may be enlarged on bail.

On the other hand, learned Additional Government Advocate for the State vehemently opposed the prayer for bail of the applicant by contending that deceased Shabbo died her unnatural death within seven years of her marriage with the applicant and as per postmortem report of the deceased she received two injuries on her body and cause of her death was asphyxia as a result of ante-mortem strangulation, but could not dispute the above factual aspect of the matter as argued on behalf of the applicant.
Having heard learned counsel for the parties and examined the matter in its entirety, I find that there are thirty-one prosecution witnesses of the charge-sheet.

Vide order dated 11.09.2024 a report was called for from the concerned Presiding Officer as to why trial of the applicant has not yet been concluded attended with further direction that the trial court shall also indicate as to whether any adjournment has been taken from the side of the applicant-Jabir during trial.

Pursuant to the aforesaid order of this Court, the trial court submitted its report dated 27.09.2024 mentioning inter alia that charge-sheet was submitted on 02.07.2021 and charge was framed on 22.07.2021, but till date, only five prosecution witnesses have been examined.
The trial court has specifically mentioned that on account of non-appearance of prosecution witnesses before the trial court, the trial of the applicant could not be concluded.
In view of the report dated 27.09.2024 of the trial court, it is clear that the applicant has fully co-operated with the trial and there is no delay on his part.
Speedy trial of the applicant is fundamental right, which is being violated in this case.

Under the circumstances as noted above, in the light of judgment of this Court in Criminal Misc.
Bail Application No. 34950 of 2024 (Manoj Vs. State of U.P.) decided on 05.12.2024, this Court feels that the applicant has made out a case for bail on the ground of long detention period and non-proceeding of the effective trial of the applicant.

Criminal Misc.
Bail Application No. 34950 of 2024 (Manoj Vs. State of U.P.)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, the bail application is hereby allowed.

Let the applicant-Jabir, be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(i) That the applicant shall cooperate with the expeditious disposal of the trial and shall regularly attend the court unless inevitable.
(ii) That the applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) That after his release, the applicant shall not involve in any criminal activity.

(iv) The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by court concerned before the release of the applicant on bail.
In case of breach of any of the conditions mentioned above, court concerned will be at liberty to cancel the bail of the applicant.

It is made clear that the observations contained in the instant order are confined to the issue of bail only and shall not affect the merit of the trial.
